threats.title: Submitted invoice content steers the approval decision
threats.description: The invoice file's contents are parsed and returned to the model as the invoice details, and a denial is followed up in the same conversation with an urgency note asking the agent to reconsider. A submitter who writes steering content into the invoice reaches the model twice with it, and the decision policy explicitly leaves the deny rules negotiable by discretion.
preconditions: the workflow relays submitted content and a reconsideration request into the model conversation
attack_path: write steering content into the submitted invoice fields
let the denial follow-up press the agent to reconsider with the content still in context
threats.impact: Invoices are approved against the stated deny rules.

threats.title: Over-ceiling invoices approved through discretionary enforcement
threats.description: The $20,000 ceiling is applied by the agent from its instructions while the schema enforces no maximum amount, and the approve rule prioritizes due-date urgency with discretion arbitrating between the rule sets. The model's approve-or-deny output is acted on as the decision with no deterministic layer holding the ceiling.
preconditions: the agent's decision is acted on without a validation step enforcing the ceiling
attack_path: submit an over-ceiling invoice with a due date inside the next week
let the urgency approve rule and discretion outweigh the deny rule
threats.impact: Payments above the stated $20,000 ceiling can be authorized.

threats.title: Submitted financial data leaves through captured traces
threats.description: Request and tool-call traces, including HTTP request and response bodies, are captured for debugging, and invoice contents are parsed and returned to the model — so the captured bodies carry submitted financial data to the observability service.
preconditions: trace capture includes request and response bodies
attack_path: read its contents from the captured request and response bodies
threats.impact: Submitted financial data is exposed through the trace store.

threats.title: Provider credentials taken from the agent runtime
threats.description: The agent runs with credentials for the model provider and the observability service. An attacker who compromises the runtime holds both; how the credentials are stored, scoped, or rotated is not described.
preconditions: an attacker reaches the agent runtime or its configuration
attack_path: call the model provider and observability service as the agent
threats.impact: Both third-party services can be used under the agent's identity.

threats.title: Forged submitter identity in an uploaded invoice
threats.description: The submitter field is a value in the uploaded document and submitters are not otherwise authenticated to the workflow. Whether anything upstream establishes who submitted is not described; a forged approved-submitter name would pass the case-insensitive list validation.
preconditions: no upstream system binds the submitter field to an authenticated identity
attack_path: write an approved submitter's name into the invoice
threats.impact: Invoices are processed under an identity the submitter does not hold.
